items.author: AdamBLiv
items.context: @AdamBLiv (Adam Livingston, 89.253 seguidores), en inglés: crecimiento interanual de la media de 200 semanas de Bitcoin medida en oro (foto del 23 de noviembre de cada año): 2020 +36%, 2021 +110%, 2022 +29%, 2023 +16%, 2024 +31%, 2025 +6,6%, 2026 +3,0%; BTC/oro spot está 24% bajo su 200WMA. «One more flat year and the trend goes…» con gráfico. Post de ~1,7 h con 64 likes, 3 reposts, 15 respuestas, 3 guardados y 4.435 vistas. Ángulo: media de 200 semanas como indicador de valoración/piso (Market Temperature).
items.suggested_text:
Pricing the 200-week average in gold strips out dollar debasement and leaves a cleaner read on real trend growth. Seen that way, the deceleration is hard to miss: +110% in 2021, then +29%, +16%, +31%, and now +6.6% and +3.0% in the last two snapshots.

The 200WMA is slow by design, roughly four years of weekly closes, so a flattening slope says the whole last cycle added very little in gold terms, not just the past few months. And with spot BTC/gold 24% below that line, the discount is wider than the dollar chart alone would suggest.

A slope near zero is exactly where a long average either gets rebuilt from below or starts rolling over, and the two paths look the same until one week they don't.
